title: After 5.0 upgrade, ngc generates invalid(?) metadata.json files for files that do not export anything

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Indicates than the issue relates to something that worked in a previous version

labels.name: area: core
labels.description: Issues related to the framework runtime

body:
## I'm submitting a... 

[ ] Regression (a behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[ x ] Bug report  
[ ] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
## Current behavior When I run ngc on my library, it generates `.metadata.json` files even for files that have no exports (previously with 4.x no metadata files were generated for such files). The content of the metadata file is just `[null]`. This causes AoT compilation (with `@ngtools/webpack`/`@angular/cli`) to throw an error: ``` ERROR in TypeError: Cannot read property 'version' of null at readMetadataFile (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler-cli\src\transformers\metadata_reader.js:66:28) at Object.readMetadata (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler-cli\src\transformers\metadata_reader.js:35:25) at TsCompilerAotCompilerTypeCheckHostAdapter.getMetadataFor (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler-cli\src\transformers\compiler_host.js:413:34) at StaticSymbolResolver.getModuleMetadata (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler\bundles\compiler.umd.js:31787:62) at StaticSymbolResolver.hasDecorators (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler\bundles\compiler.umd.js:31514:46) at analyzeFile (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler\bundles\compiler.umd.js:30061:63) at AotCompiler._analyzeFile (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler\bundles\compiler.umd.js:29289:17) at AotCompiler.findGeneratedFileNames (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler\bundles\compiler.umd.js:29305:42) at Object.findGeneratedFileNames (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler-cli\src\transformers\program.js:387:82) at TsCompilerAotCompilerTypeCheckHostAdapter.getSourceFile (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\@angular\compiler-cli\src\transformers\compiler_host.js:325:55) at findSourceFile (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\typescript\lib\typescript.js:70246:29) at processImportedModules (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\typescript\lib\typescript.js:70393:25) at findSourceFile (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\typescript\lib\typescript.js:70274:17) at processImportedModules (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\typescript\lib\typescript.js:70393:25) at findSourceFile (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\typescript\lib\typescript.js:70274:17) at processImportedModules (C:\Devel\cli-app\node_modules\typescript\lib\typescript.js:70393:25) ``` An example of file with no exports - downgrade of a service separately, because I support both hybrid and Angular 4+ only apps: ``` import { downgradeInjectable } from '@angular/upgrade/static'; import { AuthService } from '@xx/core'; declare var angular: angular.IAngularStatic; angular .module('xx.upgrade') .factory('xxAuth', downgradeInjectable(AuthService)); ``` ## Expected behavior No metadata files should be generated for these files? Not sure if this is an intended change. For now I have this workaround: ``` ngc(['-p', tsConfigPath]); const metadata = globby.sync(['dist/'**/*.metadata.json')]); for (const metadataFile of metadata) { const content = fs.readFileSync(metadataFile, { encoding: 'utf8' }); if (content === '[null]') { gutil.log('Detected invalid metadata.json files. Purging...'); fs.unlinkSync(metadataFile); } } ``` ## Environment 

Angular version: 5.0.1
